name: שְׁלֻמִיאֵל
gloss: at peace with God; or my peace is God
summary: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the prince of Simeon in the wilderness, who stood with Moses at the numbering, camped with Simeon beside Reuben, brought Simeon’s gift on the fifth day of the altar’s dedication, ending with a sacrifice of peace offerings, and led Simeon’s host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:6; 2:12; 7:36–41; 10:19). The name joins שְׁלֻמִי, the passive participle of שָׁלֵם “be at peace”, to אֵל, God: “one at peace with God”, as the wise woman calls herself one of “the peaceable (שְׁלֻמֵי), the faithful of Israel” (2Sa 20:19); or, with the ־ִי of “my”, “my peace (welfare) is God”.

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, שְׁלֻמִיאֵל son of Zurishaddai.
“For Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai”, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
The prince of the sons of Simeon, camped beside Reuben on the south.
On the fifth day Shelumiel brings Simeon’s offering.
“And for the sacrifice of peace offerings (הַשְּׁלָמִים), two oxen, five rams …: this was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai”: the root of his name in his offering.
שְׁלֻמֵי אֱמוּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, “the peaceable, the faithful of Israel”: the same participle as the first part of the name.
“Acquaint yourself with him and be at peace (וּשְׁלם)”: the qal of being at peace with God.
שׁוֹלְמִי, “the one at peace with me”.

note: BDB key v.ds.ay (Num 1:6; 2:12; 7:36, 41; 10:19). TIPNR keys Shelumiel’s tribe as Benjamin; the text makes him prince of Simeon (Num 1:6; 2:12; 7:36; 10:19). Whether שְׁלֻמִי is the participle in construct (“at peace with God”) or a noun with “my” (“my peace is God”) no verse settles; both readings are given.
